title: Introduction to the College Experience
description: An introductory course for fall quarter freshmen. Course provides new students with direction and guidance on how to be successful in higher education, and specifically, at the research university. Topics include critical thinking and reading, analytical writing, major selection, university structure, mental health and wellness, citizenship, campus resources, institutional and system-wide objectives.
prerequisites_raw: Must be a new freshman at UCSB.

title: Introduction to the University Experience
description: Introduces first-year students to the mission of the research university, the role of higher education in society and their role, as students, within the community of scholars. Topics cover academic, social and personal issues relevant to the college experience. Undergraduate research opportunities will be promoted.

title: Introduction to the Research University for International Students
description: Course introduces first-year international students to US higher education systems with a specific focus on achieving academic success at UCSB through the process of academic writing enhancement, critical thinking and exploring university resources for personal development and academic success.

title: Statistical Foundations for Human Services and Education Sciences
description: An introduction to various statistical concepts in research and evaluation related to education and applied psychology. The course covers topics that include: Descriptive Statistics, probability, sampling, hypothesis testing, inferential statistics, categorical variables, regression and correlation.

title: Current Trends in Learning and Human Development
description: Introduction to major themes and current issues in human development and learning. Featuring current research and theoretical foundations in social, cognitive, physical, linguistic, and psychological development. Content includes theory and research on psychological dimensions of children and adults in various contextual settings.

title: Learning Across the Lifespan
description: Introduces theories of learning from different perspectives – behavioral, cognitive, sociocultural, sociopolitical, neuroscience, and artificial intelligence - and explores the implications of these perspectives to understand how people learn over their lifespan in various contexts of engagement and participation.

title: Education and Human Diversity
description: Explores the neuro-biological, linguistic, developmental, and structural aspects of human diversity. Students examine how societies organize and respond to such diversity, with a focus on the role of education in shaping the social and cultural functions of diversity.

title: Educational Research in an Informed Society
description: Discusses the intersection between society and educational research, including school reform, ethnicity and race, higher education, teaching and teachers, and the curriculum. Offers an overview of educational research and introduces inquiry methods in education and social/behavioral sciences.

title: Independent Studies
description: Study of special problems in various fields of education and/or faculty supervised research assistance.

title: Technology Tools for Teachers
description: Intended for upper-division undergraduates who contemplate entering a teacher credential program. It will teach for and certify their competency in selected Technology Proficiencies required for the California Level I Teaching Credential.

title: Health Education
description: Introduces physiological, psychological, and sociological factors that promote health and prevent disease including alcohol, narcotic, drug, and tobacco abuse: nutrition, chronic and infectious diseases; reproductive health and stress management. General educational applications lectures.
prerequisites_raw: Admission to the Teacher Education Program; upper-division standing.

title: Health Education
description: Students learn about health education, theories of behavior change, and wellness resources related to nutrition, alcohol, drugs, tobacco, and sexuality. Students demonstrate their understanding of course concepts by critical analysis, papers, reports, and objective tests.

title: Introduction to Child and Adolescent Development
description: An introductory course on the development of children from infancy to adolescence. Examines developmental changes and basic developmental theories (e.g., Piaget, Vygotsky) in four general areas: cognitive, social, language, and physical development. Fulfills TEP developmental course prerequisite or Education minor.

title: Race, Inequality, and Education
description: This undergraduate level course highlights how race and racism shape education in the U.S. To do so, students learn about critical theories of race that can be used to study and understand educational inequality.

title: Motivation and Learning for Academic Success
description: Presents topics on motivation and learning that contribute to academic achievement. Students transitioning to the university will apply theory to develop effective learning, study, and self-management strategies. Designed for new transfer students taking at least 1 course in summer session.
prerequisites_raw: Course is open only to newly-admitted transfer students entering in the summer quarter. Consent of instructor.

title: The Research University and The Transfer Student Experience
description: Introduces new transfer students to the mission of the research university, the role of higher education in society and their role, as students, within the community of scholars. Topics cover academic, social and personal issues relevant to college students, specifically transfer students.
prerequisites_raw: Consent of instructor; must be a new transfer student.

title: Practicum in Teaching in Higher Education
description: A course designed for undergraduate students who were selected to serve as co-leaders in one of our large courses (ED 20, ED 118, ED 173.) Students will learn about adult development theories, pedagogical techniques, and learning assessment. Students will create lesson plans, facilitate discussions, grade assignments, and foster positive learning environments.

title: Introduction to K-12 Teaching
description: Provides students the opportunity to explore the teaching profession. Students gain firsthand experience in a local K-12 classroom, examine the California Standards for the Teaching Profession, and practice lesson planning and other fundamental aspects of the teaching profession.

title: Pre-professional Work in the K-12 Classroom
description: Students are placed in a local K-12 classroom to participate in and observe firsthand the fundamental aspects of teaching and learning. Through independent coursework, students reflect upon their classroom experiences within the framework of the California Standards for the Teaching Profession.

title: Culture, Development, and Education
description: An examination of culturally constructed beliefs, attitudes, and values. Course examines how culture shapes human development, behavior, and interpersonal relations in culturally pluralistic environments, with an emphasis on educational settings.

title: Practicum in Community Based Learning
description: Students do practicum hours in the local community and schools, read relevant articles and examine results from related research projects.

title: Schooling in the U.S.
description: A study of the relationship between school and society. Social and political influences on education historically and currently are examined as well as schools as complex organizations and their unique roles in society.

title: Social Connectedness, Motivation, and Self-Regulation in Education
description: This course explores three fundamental student needs: to be connected to others socially, to be motivated, and to be self-regulated. The course investigates how educators might address these needs, and explores how interventions might improve these student outcomes.

title: Teaching for Climate Justice and Sustainability
description: Examines the teaching of climate justice and sustainability in K-12 classrooms. It is interactive and project-based. Students will increase their understanding and use of interdisciplinary resources for taking climate action. Students from all majors are invited to enroll.

title: CalTeach, Elementary Mathematics Education
description: Introduction to learning and teaching mathematics in grades K-8. The course requires attending a weekly on-campus seminar and participating in 15 hours of field placement in a local school.

title: CalTeach, Elementary Science Education
description: Introduction to learning and teaching science in grades K-8. The course requires attending a weekly on-campus seminar and participating in 15 hours of field placement in a local school.

title: CalTeach, Secondary Mathematics Education
description: Introduction to learning and teaching mathematics in grades 7-12. The course requires attending a weekly on-campus seminar and participating in 15 hours of field placement in a local school.
